gaps.title: A canvas that animates unprompted is not followed
gaps.noPage: reader-initiated animation is pinned by test/canvas_test.go; the unprompted case is the canvasStreamEvery knob, a configuration choice rather than a parity property

gaps.title: Icon fonts ship whole, never subsetted
gaps.noPage: a byte-cost gap, not a rendering one: whether the glyphs draw at all is fonts/icon-ligature's business

gaps.title: A font registered through the FontFace API cannot ship; its glyphs render as their ligature names
gaps.notes: measured to the wall: an API face finishes loading as a paramless CSS.fontsUpdated (a CSS-declared face's event names family and src), JavaScript cannot read a FontFace's source back out of it, and the agent's isolated world does not enumerate page-realm FontFaceSet entries at all — its document.fonts sees only CSS-connected faces. What remains is reading the page's own world, which the page could detect, and the mirror's first principle is that the page never knows. The investigation still shipped one thing: CSS.fontsUpdated now feeds __skyhook.fontFaceSeen, which synthesizes a @font-face for a family whose declaring stylesheet the agent cannot read — a CDN sheet's icon font ships even when sheet recovery failed

gaps.title: wheel and hover are protocol surface no client sends
gaps.noPage: needs a pointer-move vocabulary the interaction executor does not have yet; P-115's page will carry both when it grows one

gaps.title: Password and sensitive-autocomplete values never cross the wire
The landside browser is a phone with a mouse: touch is never emulated, so maxTouchPoints is 0 and pointer-aware pages lay out differently per half
gaps.noPage: both harness browsers are mice too, so the divergence cannot arise in-corpus; imported real pages carry the widened page-height band it causes

gaps.title: File upload is not implemented
gaps.noPage: clicking a file input landside opens a native chooser nothing intercepts — the gap includes that hazard — so no safe corpus interaction exists until Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog is wired

gaps.title: Clipboard copy executes plane-side only; cross-tab paste fidelity is absent
gaps.notes: the copy leg is relayed, input-caused only: Browser.grantPermissions gives every origin the async clipboard (headless has no prompt, so ungranted meant every page Copy button rejected outright), and after replaying a click or key the agent's clipProbe reads the clipboard once and answers only with a change — seeded before it will relay anything, so whatever predates the document never crosses; nothing polls. The text travels as TypeClipboard (64 kB cap, Cause naming the input) and the shell writes it through the browser's own API inside the click's activation window, falling back to a toast whose Copy button is its own activation. Paste already worked: InText/InPaste carry the reader's text into the landside document. Chrome UI is invisible to the mirror probes, so the pins are TestACopyThePageMakesReachesTheReader and TestPWARelayedCopyLandsOnTheClipboard

gaps.title: Find-in-page has no chrome-UI affordance
gaps.noPage: a chrome-UI gap, not a mirror-rendering one

gaps.title: A frame is only preemptible between messages; a large snapshot owns the link while it sends
gaps.noPage: a latency property of the scheduler, measured by the netem suite's timings rather than by parity

gaps.title: The document is delivered whole, never viewport-first
gaps.noPage: a delivery-order property; parity measures the settled document, which is identical either way

gaps.title: A closed shadow root is invisible: such a component mirrors as its light DOM only
gaps.notes: closed means closed to the isolated world too: attachShadow's return value is the only handle, and it was handed to page script the mirror never sees. The two routes in are wrapping attachShadow before page scripts run — a main-world modification the page can detect, against the mirror's first principle — or serialising through the CDP DOM domain's pierce, which is a second, parallel serialiser for one corpus page. Both stand rejected for now; shadow/closed's geometry expectedFail pins the shape

gaps.title: Reader-preference media features are answered plane-side, so the two halves may genuinely lay out differently
prefers-color-scheme is settled landside; changing it re-snapshots every tab
srcset and sizes are dropped; one server-chosen rendition ships
An animated GIF ships its first frame only
Canvas, WebGL and video are photographs: region shots, taken after input, never live
Ad and creative networks are blocked landside, so their content never exists to mirror
Alerts, confirms and prompts are auto-accepted landside and never shown to the reader
gaps.notes: deliberate today, but confirm() answering yes to everything deserves a reader-visible affordance eventually

gaps.title: Landside scroll is matched by range fraction, so IntersectionObserver-driven lazy loading fires approximately
gaps.notes: document scrolls are now anchored, not proportional: the client names the mirrored element at its viewport top and where its box sits (ScrollEvent.Anchor/AnchorY), and the landside replay puts the same element at the same offset — exact even when the two documents differ in height, which substituted fonts alone guarantee on real pages. The range fraction remains as the fallback for an anchor a mutation has since removed, and still owns the at-the-bottom case. textmisc/scroll-lazyload pins the whole path: telemetry, anchor resolution, landside scroll, the page's IntersectionObserver firing, and the revealed text mirroring back

gaps.title: A mirrored sub-document is laid out plane-side against a box, not a viewport: reader fonts, no percentage heights, fixed and sticky resolve against the wrong thing
gaps.notes: three pieces make the stand-in behave like the viewport it replaces: layout containment on it re-homes absolute and fixed descendants that used to anchor to the bottom of the whole mirror; the shadow root's base sheet carries the sub-document twin of the margin-collapse padding (the shell's own stylesheet cannot reach past the boundary, which is why the top-document fix never applied inside frames); and data-sky-box is applied as the border box it was measured as, where content-box sizing added the stand-in's own border on top and ran every framed document 2px wide. The percentage-height chain itself already resolved — the stand-in's definite box is what 100% finds. frames/viewport-units pins all of it at zero nodes off

gaps.title: A cross-origin frame that cannot be mirrored stays a labelled box; past the depth or count limits, so does one that could be
A cross-origin frame smaller than 64x32 gets no label at all — indistinguishable from a bug
gaps.noPage: settled as the design: a frame below the label floor is an ad pixel or a tracking beacon, and naming its host would put furniture on every page that carries them. The affordance floor is FRAME_LABEL_MIN_W/H in agent.js; the frame element, its box and its src still cross, so a bundle can always tell the box from a bug

gaps.title: A select change never reaches the landside page except through a form submit
gaps.notes: fixed two-sided: the host sends a change event's selection as a setvalue (multiple selects join their values with newlines, the way submit serializes them), and the agent's setValue grew a SELECT branch that picks options through the native value setter and fires input+change. forms/select's interaction and attributes dimensions pin it

gaps.title: setvalue and blur are dispatched to the top-level agent only; a non-append edit inside a mirrored cross-origin frame is silently lost
gaps.notes: three fixes, one per leg: setvalue and blur route through evalInSlot like every other input; typed text is spliced by the frame's own agent (__skyhook.insertText) because Input.insertText only reaches the browser's focused frame, which a programmatic focus inside an inlined frame never is; and the host hands the echo the composed event target, since an input event from a sub-document's shadow root reaches the document renamed to the frame's stand-in. forms/frame-editing pins all three

gaps.title: A blob: image source serialises as a landside blob URL the client can never fetch: a broken image with no fallback and no Missing notice
gaps.notes: a blob image is described and shipped like any other; the bytes are read by an in-page fetch (Tab.fetchBlob) because only the page's own realm can resolve the URL the network stack has never heard of. A blob a frame minted, or one the page revoked before the pipeline asked, still fails — to the Missing notice now, not to a silent broken image. images/blob-src pins the working case

gaps.title: Favicons never travel: TabState.FaviconID is decoded by the client and set by nothing
gaps.notes: fixed in the same commit as P-109 (the chrome the page never carries): the agent names the page's icon — the smallest declared raster, or the /favicon.ico every browser would have asked for — the server fetches it landside, sniffs the magic bytes, and ships it inside TabState.FaviconID as a data URL; the strip seats it where the spinner goes. Chrome UI stays invisible to the mirror probes, so the pin is TestTheTabStateCarriesTheFavicon rather than a corpus page. The registry flip was missed in that commit and corrected after

gaps.title: HTML comments are never mirrored, though KindComment exists on both halves of the protocol
gaps.notes: renders nothing, so nothing is lost; kept as the record that the protocol claims surface neither end implements

gaps.title: object, embed and applet are dropped whole with no stand-in: an unexplained hole where an iframe gets a labelled box
gaps.notes: plugin containers now cross on the iframe bargain: the element (not its fallback children), its measured box, its computed display — the CSS that made it a block selects a tag the stand-in no longer answers to — and a host label when the box is big enough to owe one. textmisc/object-embed's geometry pins the healed hole

gaps.title: Dead wire surface: TypeIntegrity, OpImage and ScrollEvent.Visible are never produced or consumed
gaps.noPage: wire bookkeeping with no rendering consequence; recorded so the next protocol change deletes it rather than trips over it

gaps.title: Downloads are unhandled: a download link writes a file onto the VPS and the reader sees nothing happen
gaps.notes: a download now lands on the server first — Browser.setDownloadBehavior allowAndName into a directory of its own, each file named by GUID — and every state change is announced to every session as TypeDownload: the shelf belongs to the user, not a tab. The bytes cross the link only on an explicit, size-labelled ask (TypeDownloadCmd fetch), chunked as TypeDownloadPart on bulk where they cannot head-of-line-block a page, resumable from any offset, stoppable mid-flight; discard deletes the landside copy and the kill switch wipes the directory. The client toasts the landing, prices the fetch, and holds the file in a Transfers panel until saved. Chrome UI is invisible to the mirror probes, so the pins are e2e: TestDownloadsLandAndCrossOnAsk (protocol, both legs, second device, resume, refusal, discard) and TestPWADownloadArrivesOnAsk (the real client end to end)

gaps.title: window.open and a plain click on target=_blank open a landside tab no client tab will ever show
gaps.notes: popups are recognised at browser level by their opener — a page session's autoAttach never delivers them — and adopted as ordinary tabs (Browser.OnPopup, Session.PopupOpened): attach, mirror, announce, and snapshot the document if it settled before the agent existed (Tab.Adopted). Discovery can announce one target twice, so adoption dedups on the owned set. The reader is not switched to the new tab; a row appearing is the honest version of a window opening off-stage. nav/target-blank's shell-tab count pins it

gaps.title: There is no print path: window.print does nothing for the reader
gaps.noPage: printing is chrome UI the harness cannot see; that @media print sheets do not leak into the screen is pinned by css/layers-scope

gaps.title: mousemove-driven widgets — drag-and-drop, sliders, hover menus — have no input path
gaps.noPage: needs a pointer-move step in the interaction executor; catalogued for the executor's next revision alongside P-004

gaps.title: An audio element is photographed as a still control strip; no audio ever crosses
DPR is never applied to image transcodes or region shots: every picture is soft on a 2x or 3x screen
gaps.notes: the transcode ceiling is now in device pixels: the landside tab emulates the reader's deviceScaleFactor, so the agent's devicePixelRatio is theirs, and describeImage scales the target by it (capped 3x) — folding the density into the dimensions folds it into the cache key, so readers at different densities never collide on one rendition. Region shots were already at density for the same reason: the capture renders under the emulated scale. fit() still never upscales past the source, so 1x sources cost nothing new. Pinned by TestPicturesShipAtTheReadersDensity, which opens the same page at densities 1 and 2 and measures what arrives; the parity runner still has no dpr-2 knob, so the e2e pin is the measurement

gaps.title: A prefers-color-scheme media query nested inside a plain style rule crosses with its question intact instead of being resolved landside
gaps.notes: fixed: a style rule's own text now takes the same three passes a block shipped whole gets (shippedWhole in collectRules case 1), so a media query nested inside it is answered landside like its top-level twin; css/nesting-scheme's assertion pins it

gaps.title: The shell's font-src 'self' may refuse every blob: webfont the pipeline ships
gaps.notes: fixed: font-src gains blob:, for the same reason img-src always had it — the client rebuilds @font-face sources from bytes fetched over the protocol, and 'self' alone refused every one of them at render. fonts/faces pins it: cspViolations 1 → 0 and skyprobe now loads plane-side; the page's remaining expected failure is P-003's apiface

gaps.title: An external SVG sprite reference resolves to a URL the sandboxed frame can never fetch: the icon renders as nothing
gaps.notes: the agent fetches the sprite from inside the page — browsers require these references to be same-origin, so it always can — carries the referenced fragment on the use element (data-sky-sprite, capped at 64KB) and re-points the reference at an id of the mirror's own; the patcher scrubs the fragment of script and foreignObject and builds it into a sprite holder on the frame's root, where a resync's body swap cannot take it. images/svg-sprite pins the materialized symbol, and its corpus page now serves the sprite same-origin the way the real pattern does — the old cross-origin reference drew nothing on either half, which is why every probe used to pass over a missing icon

gaps.title: A style write onto a canvas permanently blanks its photograph until the reader touches something
gaps.notes: the audit read the comment in host.ts restyled() — 'for a canvas it is permanent' — and the measurement says otherwise: restyled() re-hangs the photograph from the held blob, and media/canvas-restyle pins that it stays painted across a style write. The comment describes only the case where the bytes never arrived; it is the stale half of this record

gaps.title: The GIF tap-to-play the transcoder's comment promises does not exist in the client
gaps.notes: the promise is now kept: the still's metadata says it was made from an animation (ImageMeta.Anim, detected by decoding the whole GIF), the context menu over such an image offers Play animation with its cost named, and the want travels as the still's key plus @anim on the ordinary want list — so the cross-flight cache holds originals exactly the way it holds renditions. The pipeline answers from the URL it remembered at transcode time and ships the fetched bytes untranscoded after sniffing them as an image; the browser plays the GIF natively. Pinned by TestATapFetchesTheOriginalAnimation

gaps.title: The mirror's own :root color and font leak into pages that rely on UA defaults
gaps.notes: fixed twice over, once in each direction: the server re-points the page's html, body and :root selectors at the data-sky-doc stamp the patcher writes on mirrored roots (rewriteRootSelectors, css.go), so page rules stop styling the frame's own elements and pouring inherited colour into the mirrored chain; and the frame's boot styles no longer set inheritable properties on its root, so the shell's chrome stops leaking downward. The agent's synthesized canvas-ground rule keeps a marker (:root[data-sky-ground]) the rewrite passes through, and the frame supplies the html,body height:100% chain deliberately that the double-match used to supply by accident. css/ua-defaults pins both directions

gaps.title: A top margin that collapses through the page's body is lost at the mirror boundary
gaps.notes: fixed: a twentieth of a pixel of padding on the mirrored html (the frame's boot styles) blocks parent-child margin collapse at exactly the boundary the real document root blocks it, so a child margin collapsing through body offsets content inside the mirrored root instead of escaping into the frame and vanishing. Rounds to zero in every probe; css/margin-collapse pins it

gaps.title: The server's echo of the reader's own focus arrives a round trip late and yanks focus back into the field they have already left
gaps.notes: the host now stamps every focus-moving input with its sequence number and each mutation carries the input that caused it, so onFocus drops a focus echo whose cause predates the last focus-moving input (host.ts applyingCause < lastFocusInputSeq): the confirmation of a field the reader already left arrives, is recognised as stale, and moves nothing.
gaps.noPage: timing-dependent by nature: the executor settles before each step so every other page measures its own gap; the guard is exercised by every interaction page's focus traffic and the fix is pinned by the staleness comparison itself

gaps.title: Top-layer state does not cross: a popover the page showed, or a modal dialog, is closed in the mirror
gaps.notes: the agent reports top-layer membership as data-sky-open — read at serialisation and kept current by capture-phase toggle/close listeners, since the events do not bubble — and the patcher reproduces it with showPopover()/showModal() in the mirror's own document, whose top layer is the frame's. textmisc/disclosure's style dimension pins the shown popover

gaps.title: In the script-disabled mirror a canvas is not a replaced element: it stretches to its container and its attribute aspect ratio scales it
gaps.notes: the patcher restates the landside intrinsic size (width/height attributes, spec defaults 300x150 absent them) as inline custom properties, and the shell's zero-specificity :where(canvas) rule renders them — so the page's own CSS still overrides the size exactly as it overrides a real canvas's intrinsic one. media/canvas and media/canvas-restyle geometry pin it

gaps.title: The document hash disagrees across languages on non-ASCII text: the agent and patcher fold UTF-16 code units while the Go replicas fold byte-indexed runes, so a healthy mirror of any page with a multi-byte character in a text node's first 32 characters reports divergence
gaps.notes: fixed: Model.Hash folds UTF-16 code units exactly as the agent and patcher do (foldHashValue, model.go). No corpus page can measure this — the browser-to-browser suite compares two JavaScript folds that always agreed — so the pin is the shared cross-language vector: TestHashMatchesTheJavaScriptConvention (internal/mirror) and the patcher's 'folds the cross-language vector' case assert the same 1767627470 over the same nodes, covering an nbsp, an em dash, a surrogate pair and clipPath's case. Discovery evidence: capture 20260820-072612 of the Hacker News front page, where both recorded hashes reproduced exactly under the two conventions

gaps.title: The mirror renders every page in standards mode: a quirks-mode page loses its quirks — table cells stop refusing the page font, and the geometry cascade follows
gaps.notes: the snapshot now carries the landside parser's verdict (Snapshot.quirks — document.compatMode, not doctype presence, because an archaic doctype still parses into quirks), and the host re-opens the mirror's document without the doctype when it differs: compatMode is fixed at parse, so the rebuild is the mechanism, and it rewires everything the open wiped. real/hn-front's style dimension — 53 differing nodes, every table cell's font — pins the fix at zero. The one residue is catalogued as P-130. A frame whose mode differs from its top document's still renders in the top document's mode: one plane document has one parser

gaps.title: A shorthand property set with var() loses its longhands in used-CSS extraction: the CSSOM serialises them as empty strings, the wire carries “border-top-color: ;”, and the mirror's parser drops the declarations
gaps.notes: fixed: when a rule's cssText carries the empty-declaration signature, the agent heals it from the sheet's authored source text — a <style>'s text synchronously, a linked sheet's via an in-page fetch prefetched at startup — locating the rule by normalised selector and ordinal and believing the candidate only if it reproduces every declaration the broken serialisation still carried (healedRuleText, agent.js). css/var-shorthand pins the heal; the wikipedia page's figure borders were the discovering case

gaps.title: The isolated-world injection race can leave a navigated tab unmirrored: when ensureWorld loses to a navigation and the settle-time retries lose too, the mirror keeps a three-node about:blank document while the page renders fully landside
gaps.notes: hardened in three places, because the race has three ways to stick: an injection that fails no longer leaves its context id stored (forgetWorld — a world without its agent answered "__skyhook is not defined" for ever); the navigation and load paths retry world setup with spaced attempts abandoned when the page moves on (ensureWorldRetry); and eval itself rebuilds once when Chromium says the context is gone (deadContext), because createIsolatedWorld can bind the document being replaced and the stored id dies with it — the rebuilt world binds the document that is actually there, and the fresh agent snapshots itself on arrival
gaps.noPage: a CDP timing race, not reproducible by a corpus page on demand. Evidence from the thirty-article conformance sweep: bundle 00 (expectedNodes 3, agent.json started:false against a fully rendered page.html) and bundle 16 (the re-injected agent answers an empty fingerprint and serverHash 2166136261 — the bare FNV basis — while the 2068-node document it sent earlier renders plane-side); seven 'isolated world setup failed' warnings in one hour of local captures, most of which recovered on a later retry

gaps.title: The three fingerprint writers disagree at the edges: DOM nodeType against protocol kind for container roots, lowercased names against clipPath, 32 UTF-16 units against 32 runes
gaps.notes: fixed: the writers now share one vocabulary — protocol kinds (the agent maps a sub-frame document to the wire's fragment kind), ASCII-lowercased element names (unifying also the patcher's docHash, which had folded wire-case clipPath and would have disagreed with a healthy agent), and values cut at 32 UTF-16 code units, backing off a split surrogate pair (fingerprintWindow in agent.js and patcher.ts, HashValueWindow in model.go, modelFingerprint in the Go client). bundle triage keeps its tolerant comparator for bundles written before the fix

gaps.title: A collapsed-border table sizes its caption differently when its borders arrive after first layout: the mirrored figure runs 2px wide and a paragraph wrapping around the float re-wraps
gaps.notes: exposed by P-126's heal on real/wikipedia-article: with the caption borders restored, the mirrored thumbnail figure measures 262px against 260 landside — under every probed computed property agreeing, border-collapse and display:table included — and the two-pixel float difference re-wraps the lead paragraph, shifting 17 inline boxes by up to 135px. A fully static render of the same computed inputs measures identically in both nested and top-level contexts, so the leading suspect is Chromium's incremental table relayout when borders and image blobs arrive after the first pass — the same page settled to landside-equal coordinates when the heal arrived late rather than early. Deterministic across runs; the wikipedia page's geometry expectedFail pins the shape

gaps.title: A quirks-mode body stretches to the viewport minus its own margins landside; the mirrored body is an inner box, and CSS cannot state a margin-box stretch for it
gaps.notes: the residue of P-125's fix: with the mirror re-parsed into quirks mode, the mirrored html restates the root's viewport stretch with min-height:100%, but the body's version of the same quirk subtracts its own margins — 709px inside a 725px viewport with default 8px margins — and no static rule can say "fill your parent's content box minus your own margin box" for an ordinary block. A percentage min-height on the body resolves to the full 100% in quirks and overshoots by exactly the margins. real/hn-front's geometry expectedFail pins the single-node shape; every content row inside the body measures landside-equal
